posts.vo: If betting odds confuse you, this takes thirty seconds. Plus one-fifty: bet a hundred to win one-fifty. Minus one-fifty: bet one-fifty to win a hundred. Plus is the underdog, minus is the favorite. Every price is really a probability. Plus one-fifty implies forty percent. Minus one-fifty implies sixty. You only have an edge when you think the real chance is higher than the price implies. Edgelytic

posts.vo: Every bet you make has a hidden fee. It's called the vig. Minus one-ten on both sides means each side implies fifty-two point four percent. Add them up: one oh four point eight. That extra is the book's cut, about four and a half percent. So at minus one-ten, you have to win fifty-two point four percent of your bets just to break even. posts.vo: Why is minus two and a half so different from minus three? Key numbers. Football scores come in threes and sevens, so more NFL games land on a three point margin than any other. Seven is next. That's why minus two and a half and minus three and a half are worlds apart. One wins on a three point game, the other loses.
